data.hypothesis: Reseeding a forward power recurrence every eight terminal indices should reduce powf calls from 64 to 8 per input while limiting each recurrence segment to at most seven multiplications. The shorter segments are intended to limit rounding drift near the payoff floor; boundary accuracy and any whole-call speedup remain unverified, and rollback may dominate total runtime.
data.notes: Only the baseline is measured: mean full-call time 0.3909827 s across three samples and correctness on eight supplied cases. No candidate timing or failed numerical variant is available yet. The controller should check varied and near-boundary inputs against tolerance and measure full-call timing; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Partition terminal indices into eight-index blocks; compute each block's unchanged starting exponent with powf, then generate the next seven powers by multiplying by u*u.
Preserve the max(0, X-S*upow) payoff floor for all 64 entries and leave rollback unchanged.
